title: अंश २ · अध्याय ९

items.speaker: श्रीपारशर उवाच
items.text:
तारामयं भगवतः शिशुमाराकृति प्रभोः ।
दिवि रूपं हरेर्यत्तु तस्य पुच्छे स्थितो ध्रुवः ॥ २,९.१ ॥
items.tr:
tārāmayaṃ bhagavataḥ śiśumārākṛti prabhoḥ |
divi rūpaṃ hareryattu tasya pucche sthito dhruvaḥ || 2,9.1 ||

items.text:
सैष भ्रमन् भ्रामयति चन्द्रादित्यादिकान् ग्रहान् ।
भ्रमन्तमनु तं यान्ति नक्षत्राणि च चक्रवत् ॥ २,९.२ ॥
items.tr:
saiṣa bhraman bhrāmayati candrādityādikān grahān |
bhramantamanu taṃ yānti nakṣatrāṇi ca cakravat || 2,9.2 ||

items.text:
सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ तारा नक्षत्राणि ग्रहैः सह ।
वातानीकमयैर्बन्धैर्ध्रुवे बद्धानि तानि वै ॥ २,९.३ ॥
items.tr:
sūryācandramasau tārā nakṣatrāṇi grahaiḥ saha |
vātānīkamayairbandhairdhruve baddhāni tāni vai || 2,9.3 ||

items.text:
शिशुमाराकृति प्रोक्तं यद्रूपं ज्योतिषां दिवि ।
नारायणोऽयनं धाम्नां तस्याधारः स्वयं हृदि ॥ २,९.४ ॥
items.tr:
śiśumārākṛti proktaṃ yadrūpaṃ jyotiṣāṃ divi |
nārāyaṇo'yanaṃ dhāmnāṃ tasyādhāraḥ svayaṃ hṛdi || 2,9.4 ||

items.text:
उत्तानपादपुत्रस्तु तमाराध्य जगत्पतिम् ।
स तारा शिशुमारस्य ध्रुवः पुच्छे व्यवस्थितः ॥ २,९.५ ॥
items.tr:
uttānapādaputrastu tamārādhya jagatpatim |
sa tārā śiśumārasya dhruvaḥ pucche vyavasthitaḥ || 2,9.5 ||

items.text:
आधारः शिशुमारस्य सर्वाध्यक्षो जनार्दनः ।
ध्रुवस्य शिशुमारस्तु ध्रुवे भानुर्व्यवस्थितः ॥ २,९.६ ॥
items.tr:
ādhāraḥ śiśumārasya sarvādhyakṣo janārdanaḥ |
dhruvasya śiśumārastu dhruve bhānurvyavasthitaḥ || 2,9.6 ||

items.text: तदाधारं जगच्चेदं सदेवासुरमानुषम् ॥ २,९.७ ॥
items.tr: tadādhāraṃ jagaccedaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam || 2,9.7 ||

items.text:
येन विप्रविधानेन तन्ममैकमनाः शृणु ।
विवस्वानष्टभिर्मासैरादायापो रसात्मिकाः ।
वर्षत्यम्बुततश्चान्नमन्नादप्यखिलं जगत् ॥ २,९.८ ॥
items.tr:
yena vipravidhānena tanmamaikamanāḥ śṛṇu |
vivasvānaṣṭabhirmāsairādāyāpo rasātmikāḥ |
varṣatyambutataścānnamannādapyakhilaṃ jagat || 2,9.8 ||

items.text:
विवस्वानंशुभिस्तीक्ष्णैरादाय जगतो जलम् ।
सोमं पुष्णात्यथेन्दुश्च वायुनाडीमयैर्दिवि ।
नालैर्विक्षिपतेऽभ्रेषु धूमाग्न्यनिलमूर्तिषु ॥ २,९.९ ॥
items.tr:
vivasvānaṃśubhistīkṣṇairādāya jagato jalam |
somaṃ puṣṇātyathenduśca vāyunāḍīmayairdivi |
nālairvikṣipate'bhreṣu dhūmāgnyanilamūrtiṣu || 2,9.9 ||

items.text:
न भ्रश्यन्ति यतस्तेभ्यो जलान्यभ्राणि तान्यतः ।
अभ्रस्थाः प्रपतन्त्यापो वायुना समुदीरिताः ।
संस्कारं कालजनितं मैत्रेयासाद्य निर्मलाः ॥ २,९.१० ॥
items.tr:
na bhraśyanti yatastebhyo jalānyabhrāṇi tānyataḥ |
abhrasthāḥ prapatantyāpo vāyunā samudīritāḥ |
saṃskāraṃ kālajanitaṃ maitreyāsādya nirmalāḥ || 2,9.10 ||

items.text:
सरित्समुद्रभौमास्तु तथापः प्राणिसम्भवाः ।
चतुष्प्रकारा भगवानादत्ते सविता मुने ॥ २,९.११ ॥
items.tr:
saritsamudrabhaumāstu tathāpaḥ prāṇisambhavāḥ |
catuṣprakārā bhagavānādatte savitā mune || 2,9.11 ||

items.text:
आकाशगङ्गासलिलं तथादायगभस्तिमान् ।
अनभ्रगतमेवोर्व्यां सद्यः क्षिपति रश्मिभिः ॥ २,९.१२ ॥
items.tr:
ākāśagaṅgāsalilaṃ tathādāyagabhastimān |
anabhragatamevorvyāṃ sadyaḥ kṣipati raśmibhiḥ || 2,9.12 ||

items.text:
तस्य संस्पर्शनिर्धूतपापपङ्को द्विजोत्तम ।
न याति नरकं मर्त्यो दिव्यं स्नानं हि तत्स्मृतम् ॥ २,९.१३ ॥
items.tr:
tasya saṃsparśanirdhūtapāpapaṅko dvijottama |
na yāti narakaṃ martyo divyaṃ snānaṃ hi tatsmṛtam || 2,9.13 ||

items.text:
दृष्टसूर्यं हि यद्वारि पतत्यभ्रैर्विना दिवः ।
आकाशगङ्गासलिलं तद्गोभिः क्षिप्यते रवेः ॥ २,९.१४ ॥
items.tr:
dṛṣṭasūryaṃ hi yadvāri patatyabhrairvinā divaḥ |
ākāśagaṅgāsalilaṃ tadgobhiḥ kṣipyate raveḥ || 2,9.14 ||

items.text:
कृत्तिकादिषु ऋक्षेषु विषमेषु च यद्दिवः ।
दृष्टार्कपतितं ज्ञेयं तद्गाङ्गं दिग्गजोज्झितम् ॥ २,९.१५ ॥
items.tr:
kṛttikādiṣu ṛkṣeṣu viṣameṣu ca yaddivaḥ |
dṛṣṭārkapatitaṃ jñeyaṃ tadgāṅgaṃ diggajojjhitam || 2,9.15 ||

items.text:
युग्मर्क्षेषु च यत्तोयं पतत्यर्कोज्झितं दिवः ।
तत्सूर्यरश्मिभिः सर्वं समादाय निरस्यते ॥ २,९.१६ ॥
items.tr:
yugmarkṣeṣu ca yattoyaṃ patatyarkojjhitaṃ divaḥ |
tatsūryaraśmibhiḥ sarvaṃ samādāya nirasyate || 2,9.16 ||

items.text:
उभयं पुण्यमत्यर्थं नृणां पापभयापहम् ।
आकाशगङ्गासलिलं दिव्यं स्नानं महामुने ॥ २,९.१७ ॥
items.tr:
ubhayaṃ puṇyamatyarthaṃ nṛṇāṃ pāpabhayāpaham |
ākāśagaṅgāsalilaṃ divyaṃ snānaṃ mahāmune || 2,9.17 ||

items.text:
यत्तु मैघैः समुत्सृष्टं वारि तत्प्राणिनां द्विज ।
पुष्णात्यौषधयः सर्वा जीवनायामृतं हि तत् ॥ २,९.१८ ॥
items.tr:
yattu maighaiḥ samutsṛṣṭaṃ vāri tatprāṇināṃ dvija |
puṣṇātyauṣadhayaḥ sarvā jīvanāyāmṛtaṃ hi tat || 2,9.18 ||

items.text:
तेन वृद्धिं परां नीतः सकलश्चौषधीगणः ।
साधकः फलपाकन्तः प्रजानां द्विज जायते ॥ २,९.१९ ॥
items.tr:
tena vṛddhiṃ parāṃ nītaḥ sakalaścauṣadhīgaṇaḥ |
sādhakaḥ phalapākantaḥ prajānāṃ dvija jāyate || 2,9.19 ||

items.text:
तेन यज्ञान्यथाप्रोक्तान्मानवाः शास्त्रचक्षुषः ।
कुर्वन्त्यहरहस्तैश्च देवानाप्याययन्तिते ॥ २,९.२० ॥
items.tr:
tena yajñānyathāproktānmānavāḥ śāstracakṣuṣaḥ |
kurvantyaharahastaiśca devānāpyāyayantite || 2,9.20 ||

items.text:
एवं यज्ञाश्च वेदाश्च वर्णाश्च द्विजपूर्वकाः ।
सर्वे देवनिकायाश्च सर्वे भूतगणाश्च ये ॥ २,९.२१ ॥
items.tr:
evaṃ yajñāśca vedāśca varṇāśca dvijapūrvakāḥ |
sarve devanikāyāśca sarve bhūtagaṇāśca ye || 2,9.21 ||

items.text:
वृष्ट्या धृतमिदं सर्वमन्नं निष्पाद्यते यया ।
सापि निष्पाद्यते वृष्टिः सवित्रा मुनिसत्तम ॥ २,९.२२ ॥
items.tr:
vṛṣṭyā dhṛtamidaṃ sarvamannaṃ niṣpādyate yayā |
sāpi niṣpādyate vṛṣṭiḥ savitrā munisattama || 2,9.22 ||

items.text:
आधारभूतः सवितुर्ध्रुवो मुनिवरोत्तम ।
ध्रुवस्य शिशुपारोऽसौ सोऽपि नारायणात्मकः ॥ २,९.२३ ॥
items.tr:
ādhārabhūtaḥ saviturdhruvo munivarottama |
dhruvasya śiśupāro'sau so'pi nārāyaṇātmakaḥ || 2,9.23 ||

items.text:
हृदि नारायणस्तस्य शिशुमारस्यं संस्थितः ।
बिभर्ता सर्वभूतानामादिभूतः सनातनः ॥ २,९.२४ ॥
items.tr:
hṛdi nārāyaṇastasya śiśumārasyaṃ saṃsthitaḥ |
bibhartā sarvabhūtānāmādibhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ || 2,9.24 ||

en_chapter: Parāçara said:—The form of the glorious Hari containing the constellations, in the shape of a porpoise in the tail of which is attached Dhruva, is seen in heaven. As Dhruva revolves, it makes the moon, the sun and stars to revolve also, and all the planets follow in its circular path; for the sun, moon and all the luminaries are in sooth tied to the polar star by aerial cords. The porpoise figure of the celestial sphere, which has been described by me to you, is upheld by Nārāyana, who himself, the source of all radiance, is seated in its heart. And having worshipped the lord of people, Dhruva, the son of Uttānpāda shines in the tail of the steller porpoise. Janārddana, the lord of all, is the supporter of this porpoise-shaped sphere—and this sphere is the supporter of Dhruva; and by Dhruva the sun is upheld. O Brahman, I shall describe how this earth is upheld by the sun; do thou listen to it attentively.

During eight months of the year the sun attracts the waters of the earth, and during the remaining four months he pours them upon the earth: from rain grows corn and by corn the whole world is upheld. The sun absorbs the moisture of the earth by means of his scorching rays and nourishes the moon thereby. And the moon through tubes of air distributes them to the clouds which are made of smoke, fire and wind. The clouds are called Abhras because their contents are not dispersed. The waters in the clouds, being driven by the wind, and freed from impurities by the sweetening process of the time, descend (upon earth), O Maitreya. The glorious sun, O Maitreya, exhales moisture from four sources, namely—seas, rivers, the earth and the living creatures. He immediately pours down on earth, without turning it into cloud, the water that he absorbs from Gangā of the skies, and people who are touched by this water are freed from all iniquities and are not constrained to see hell. This is called celestial ablution. When the sun comes in view and the water comes down from the sky without cloud then the waters of the Gangā in the skies are sprinkled by the rays of the sun. And the water that falls from the sky when the sun is in the mansion of Kirtikā and the other asterisms counted by odd numbers, the water of the Gangā is scattered by the elephants of the spheres. The water, that falls from the bright and cloudless sky when the sun is in the mansion of Rohini and other even asterisms, is distributed by his own beams. O twice-born one, both the waters are holy and they wash away the sins of the people: it is the water of the Gangā in the skies and is termed celestial ablution.

The water that the clouds distribute upon earth is in fact the ambrosia of living beings, for it sustains the plants which are the support of their existence. By this water all vegetables grow and are matured and become the means of bringing about the well being of mankind, seen and unseen. Those men, who have got holy scriptures as their eyes, perform sacrifices with them and give gratification to the celestials. In this wise all sacrifices, all celestials, Brāhmanas and other castes, all infernal creatures, all animals and the whole world are supported by the rains which produce food. O great Muni, this rain, which is the source of manifold blessings, proceeds from the sun. And the sun, O foremost of Munis, is upheld by Dhruva, which is again supported by the porpoise-shaped sphere which is at one with Nārāyana; for the ever-existing glorious Nārāyana, the supporter of the universe and the primary deity, is seated in the heart of the porpoise-shaped steller sphere.
